doc.title: Tommy Newsom and Ross Tompkins interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995

title: Tonight Show and playing the Half Note
summary: Ross joined the Tonight Show in 1967 under Doc Severinsen but kept playing clubs like the Half Note; his cab fare remark.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Yeah, I always play even, well Tommy was with the Tonight Show before I was. He was there with Skitch Henderson and Milton DeLugg. I started when Doc Severinsen started in 1967. But I always went right from there down and played someplace else. If it wasn’t the Half Note it was the Roosevelt Grill or something or the Plaza Nine. There was always some clubs.

Yeah, I asked Ross one day, you know because you spend your whole life working in gin mills and things, you know, low paying jobs, but the jazz scene is usually not high paying generally. And I asked him why he continued to work like down at the Half Note, down in the Village during the Tonight Show. Because you know you work all those years and you’ve got a nice paying job more or less, and he continued to work down there. And I think he explained it this way, he says, “I work at NBC to get cab fare to get down to the village.”
Oh, yeah, I forgot about that. Thank you. One of my better remarks.
It must have been in your blood, right? You couldn’t stop doing it. Well that’s great.
Well you know he was dedicated to playing. That’s what he really wanted to do. And I really did too but I didn’t have guts enough to — I got sidetracked with the writing and I had a lot of hats on.
